question.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations: $$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2t+1\end{aligned}] $$ The complementary solution to this system is given by $$ {x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R. $$ Then, the general solution of the system is
$x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+\,\,$ $3/2$ $\,\,t+\,\,$ {{field-1}} .
{{field-2}} $1/2$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2t+1\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is polynomial of degree $1.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also polynomial of degree $1,$ i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2}$  are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of ${x}_{p}$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{x}_{p}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the unknown constants, we substitute ${x}_{p}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}])+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2t+1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}+3{a}_{2} \\ {a}_{1}-{a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1}+3{b}_{2} \\ {b}_{1}-{b}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2t+1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0t+{a}_{1} \\ 0t+{a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}({a}_{1}+3{a}_{2})t+({b}_{1}+3{b}_{2}+1) \\ ({a}_{1}-{a}_{2}-2)t+({b}_{1}-{b}_{2}+1)\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}+3{a}_{2}=0 \\ {a}_{1}-{a}_{2}-2=0 \\ {b}_{1}+3{b}_{2}+1={a}_{1} \\ {b}_{1}-{b}_{2}+1={a}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first two equations, we get 

$$
{a}_{1}=\frac{3}{2},\,{a}_{2}=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

 
Substituting these into the third and fourth equations, and solving for ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2},$ we have

$$
{b}_{1}=-1,\,{b}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

 

Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}3/2 \\ -1/2\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1/2\end{aligned}].
$$
